bites.headline: What’s at stake
bites.body: This course tries to answer these questions and many others, providing a comprehensive overview of the scientific study of thought and behavior.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Introduction
bites.body: Professor Paul Bloom welcomes students and presents the course as a comprehensive introduction to the study of the human mind.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Introduction
bites.body: Course readings and requirements are discussed.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: The five main branches of psychology are presented: neuroscience, which is a study of the mind by looking at the brain; developmental, which focuses on how people grow and learn; cognitive, which refers to the computational approach to…
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Foundations: This Is Your Brain
bites.body: This lecture introduces students to two broad theories of how the mind relates to the body.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Foundations
bites.body: Dualism is the ubiquitous and intuitive feeling that our conscious mind is separate from our physical bodies, whereas Materialism is the idea that all of our mental states are caused by physical states of the brain.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: This discussion is followed by a basic overview of the neurophysiology of the brain.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Foundations: Freud
bites.body: This lecture introduces students to the theories of Sigmund Freud, including a brief biographical description and his contributions to the field of psychology.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Foundations
bites.body: The limitations of his theories of psychoanalysis are covered in detail, as well as the ways in which his conception of the unconscious mind still operate in mainstream psychology today.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: The limitations of his theories of psychoanalysis are covered in detail, as well as the ways in which his conception of the unconscious mind still operate in mainstream psychology today.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Foundations: Skinner
bites.body: Professor Bloom opens with a brief discussion of the value and evolutionary basis of unconscious processing.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Foundations
bites.body: The rest of this lecture introduces students to the theory of Behaviorism, particularly the work of prominent behaviorist, B.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Different types of learning are discussed in detail, as well as reasons why behaviorism has been largely displaced as an adequate theory of human mental life.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: What Is It Like to Be a Baby: The Development of Thought
bites.body: This lecture explores issues and ideas related to the branch of psychology known as cognitive development.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: This
bites.body: It begins with an introduction of Piaget who, interested in the emergence of knowledge in general, studied children and the way they learn about the world in order to formulate his theories of cognitive development.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Finally, the question of the relationship between and the existence of different kinds of development is addressed.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: How Do We Communicate?: Language in the Brain, Mouth and the Hands
bites.body: One of the most uniquely human abilities is the capacity for creating and understanding language.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: One
bites.body: This lecture introduces students to the major topics within the study of language: phonology, morphology, syntax and recursion.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: This lecture also describes theories of language acquisition, arguments for the specialization of language, and the commonalities observed in different languages across cultures.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Conscious of the Present; Conscious of the Past: Language (cont.); Vision and Memory
bites.body: This lecture finishes the discussion of language by briefly reviewing two additional topics: communication systems in non-human primates and other animals, and the relationship between language and thought.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: This
bites.body: The majority of this lecture is then spent on introducing students to major theories and discoveries in the fields of perception, attention and memory.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Topics include why we see certain visual illusions, why we don't always see everything we think we see, and the relationship between different types of memory.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Conscious of the Present; Conscious of the Past: Vision and Memory (cont.)
bites.body: In this lecture, Professor Bloom reviews the basic psychological research on memory.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Professor
bites.body: Specific topics covered include the different memory types, memory limitations, strategies that improve memory, and memory disorders.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: This lecture also includes a discussion of several important social implications for memory research, such as recovered memories, and the influence of suggestibility on eyewitness testimony.
bites.attribution_line: Paul Bloom, Introduction to Psychology (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/introduction-psychology/psyc-110 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA
